episodes.211746: A strong short wave trough approaching the area on the afternoon of the tenth combined with a potent cold front to create severe convection. Strong instability above the frontal zone allowed for storms to become severe in the southern Rolling Plains. One storm produced up to two inch size hail as it moved over Lake Alan Henry (Garza County).
episodes.211792: Isolated thunderstorms move southeast across the eastern Colorado plains during the late afternoon and evening of May 9th. Wind gusts up to 70 mph accompanied the stronger thunderstorms.
episodes.211863: A cold front swept through the region Sunday. Meanwhile, a shortwave neared from the west. These sources of lift allowed for thunderstorms to develop across the Western Low Rolling Plains and the eastern Permian Basin. These thunderstorms produced very large hail, up to the size of baseballs. Meanwhile, as the front swept through the area high winds were recorded at a couple of Mesonet sites in west Texas and southeast New Mexico.
episodes.212533: Multiple rounds of storms moved over portions of SE Texas, bringing large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.213022: Over Mother's Day weekend, a slow-moving cold front triggered scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across North and Central Texas. The majority of these storms occurred on Mother's Day (May 10), with many reaching severe levels and large hail becoming the most frequent report. Hail up to 4.5 was reported in Hamilton County.
episodes.213252: A line of storms crossed over the Eastern Great Lakes and moved into the Niagara Frontier to Genesee Valley producing sporadic reports of damaging winds.
episodes.213311: Warm, moist air combined with the influence of a dryline located across the eastern portion of the Texas Panhandle. This resulted in the development of an isolated thunderstorm during the evening of May 9th. With enough cold air present in the upper atmosphere, this allowed for large hail to grow within the storm and fall across portions of eastern Texas Panhandle. Additional storms developed during the early morning hours of May 10th along a southward moving cold front. These early morning storms produced hail between 1 and 1.5 over the northeastern combined Panhandles.
episodes.213366: The passage of a southeastward-moving upper system (and associated surface front) fostered scattered severe thunderstorms during the evening of the 9th, focused across portions of western Oklahoma. Large to very large hail was the main storm hazard amid steep lapse rates and strong wind shear, sufficient for supercells. Focused areas of wind damage occurred near Sayre and northeast of Lawton as well.
episodes.213437: An isolated thunderstorm moved southeast across northeast and east-central Colorado during the evening hours of May 9th, ahead of an approaching cold front. Wind gusts up to 71 mph were measured in Kit Carson County, with one inch diameter hail in Yuma County.
episodes.213447: Late evening convection initiated along a southeastward moving cold front in a broken line. Marginal MLCAPE values up to 500 J/kg with 30-40 knots of line-normal effective shear produced sporadic wind damage in northwestern PA with reports of trees down.
episodes.213910: A northwest flow aloft was in place across the Four State Region during the morning of May 10th, developing on the east side of an upper level ridge of high pressure over the Rockies and Desert Southwest. A shortwave trough embedded in this flow regime traversed the Oklahoma/Texas Panhandle during the early morning hours, before moving into East Texas by late morning and North Louisiana during the afternoon. Diurnal heating contributed to an unstable air mass by late morning/early afternoon, with the approaching trough helping to enhance large scale forcing for the development of scattered severe thunderstorms across portions of East Texas and North Louisiana, where multiple reports of large hail and damaging winds were received. These storms eventually exited the region by late afternoon with the departure of this disturbance aloft.
episodes.213911: A northwest flow aloft was in place across the Four State Region during the morning of May 10th, developing on the east side of an upper level ridge of high pressure over the Rockies and Desert Southwest. A shortwave trough embedded in this flow regime traversed the Oklahoma/Texas Panhandle during the early morning hours, before moving into East Texas by late morning and North Louisiana during the afternoon. Diurnal heating contributed to an unstable air mass by late morning/early afternoon, with the approaching trough helping to enhance large scale forcing for the development of scattered severe thunderstorms across portions of East Texas and North Louisiana, where multiple reports of large hail and damaging winds were received. These storms eventually exited the region by late afternoon with the departure of this disturbance aloft.
episodes.214028: The combination of multiple frontal boundaries draped across central Arkansas in cohesion with approaching H500 troughs led to an atmosphere that was conducive for the development of multiple storms across the state. The majority of these isolated storms would remain strong, but a few managed to become severe producing a few instances of severe wind gusts and large hail. Additionally, as cold air aloft remained increasingly cold and air at the surface became increasingly hot multiple cold air funnels were noted with a few strong thunderstorms across the state.
episodes.214031: On the afternoon and evening of Saturday, May 9, 2026, a line of thunderstorms swept across Lake Erie, Northern Ohio, and Northwest Pennsylvania. Within this line, several severe thunderstorms produced marine wind gusts, wind gusts over land, and wind damage over land areas.
episodes.214039: On the afternoon and evening of Saturday, May 9, 2026, a line of thunderstorms swept across Lake Erie, several severe thunderstorms produced marine wind gusts.
episodes.214060: The combination of a dryline and cold front along with strong instability resulted in scattered severe thunderstorms across much of the area. The strongest storms produced very large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.214075: A cold front stalled across the region while multiple short waves moved overhead. This produce multiple days of unsettled weather.
episodes.214133: An occluding low pressure system to the northwest in Quebec, bringing a strong cold front through Maine on the evening of May 10th. There was a period of clearing ahead of the frontal system, allowing instability to increase and storms to develop. Thunderstorms moved into Aroostook county by early evening. Favorable instability helped an organized line of storms to develop, which bring elevated wind gusts and heavy rainfall. Low-level mesovortex within the line produced a microburst in the Caribou area, causing significant damage to a locally confined region. Multiple trees were reported down in woman's backyard, along with structural damage to outdoor structures.
episodes.214245: A lingering convective complex from the prior evening (9th), along with modest warm ascent, fostered continued strong thunderstorm activity across portions of southern Oklahoma during the morning of the 10th. A few stronger thunderstorm cores produced reports of small hail.
episodes.214266: A line of storms crossed over the Eastern Great Lakes and moved into the region producing sporadic reports of damaging winds.
episodes.214325: Multiple thunderstorms produced strong to severe wind gusts along the coast.
episodes.214326: Multiple thunderstorms produced severe conditions along the Brevard and Volusia County coasts.
episodes.214407: Boundary collisions over the interior of South Florida allowed for strong thunderstorms to develop over Lake Okeechobee late afternoon into the evening on May 10th, 2026.
